headline: OpenAI reportedly completed a $7 billion employee tender offer at an $852B valuation
summary: OpenAI's tender offer, valued at $852 billion, provides liquidity to employees but may signal a delay in the company's anticipated IPO.
details: OpenAI has reportedly completed a $7 billion tender offer, buying back shares from employees to provide liquidity. This deal values the privately held AI lab at $852 billion, matching its most recent fundraising round in March.

The company had confidentially filed with the SEC in June to prepare for a potential IPO later this year. However, a tender offer often suggests that a public offering may not be imminent, allowing employees to realize stock value without a full IPO.

This move comes as CEO Sam Altman stated the company is 'about to have our best 12 months to date,' despite reportedly missing internal financial goals earlier this year. Firms going public typically want to show strong financial results to investors.

With rival Anthropic reportedly profitable, OpenAI may be ensuring it presents its best financial face. The tender could indicate a strategic wait for its new focus on enterprise business to gain traction before a public debut.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI launches GPT-5.6-Cyber]] with 95% completion on advanced cybersecurity tasks
headline: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6-Cyber with 95% completion on advanced cybersecurity tasks
summary: This specialized model, a fine-tuned version of GPT-5.6 Sol, is designed for advanced vulnerability research and exploit development, significantly reducing refusals on high-risk tasks. Access is limited to approved organizations via the new Daybreak Red progr
details: OpenAI has launched GPT-5.6-Cyber, a specialized model for advanced vulnerability research and exploit development. It handles categories of work its general-purpose models often refuse, achieving 95% completion on advanced cybersecurity tasks.
This model is a fine-tuned version of OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, unveiled in June. It was specifically trained to improve performance in finding zero-day vulnerabilities and developing exploit chains.

Crucially, GPT-5.6-Cyber was also trained to reduce refusals on "dual-use" cybersecurity requests, which can serve both legitimate defensive and malicious offensive purposes. Its 95% completion rate on internal benchmarks compares to 57.3% for GPT-5.5-Cyber and just 1.5% for the standard GPT-5.6 Sol.
Access to GPT-5.6-Cyber is not broadly available. Organizations must be accepted into the new Daybreak Red tier of OpenAI’s Daybreak cybersecurity program to gain access.

Daybreak Red is intended for approved security teams conducting advanced, authorized cyber work, such as penetration testing, red-team exercises, and exploit validation on owned systems. This ensures the model is used by trusted defenders with a clear professional need.
OpenAI also introduced Daybreak Blue, a broader tier offering vetted users access to general models like GPT-5.6 Sol with adjusted guardrails for legitimate defensive work, but without GPT-5.6-Cyber.

Pricing for GPT-5.6-Cyber is set at $12.50 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens. This makes it more expensive than GPT-5.6 Sol, which is priced at $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens in the same program.

Enterprises seeking access must apply through Daybreak Access, providing details on their security work, usage plans, and confirming lawful, defensive, and authorized use. Applicants also need to demonstrate a robust security program with controls like SSO, MFA, role-based access, and recognized security certifications.
